title: On Looking for the key in every room
subtitle: 仪表穿着 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 仪表穿着（人与自我·生活与学习·个人仪表与穿着）
meta: 主题语境：仪表穿着（人与自我·生活与学习·个人仪表与穿着）　|　核心词汇：look　|　正文 353 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 look 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1955 the trader ① looked for the key in every room twice over, and every partner in the market said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three weeks on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the trader ② looks for the key in every room year after year without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ look for the key in every room at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ looked for the key in every room before — a line in the list for October 1949 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Looking for the key in every room twice over, the trader said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the basket at the far stall, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ look older than his forty years year after year, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Look older than his forty years at once and never mention it again.

By 1962 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the list, and a new partner from the next market ⑧ looks older than his forty years twice over every week without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the stall, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ looked for the key in every room again when nobody else would.

⑩ To look for the key in every room, my mother said in 1967, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the market remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the market forgets, somebody looks for the key in every room year after year again and somebody must look for the key in every room twice over all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 看（一般过去式 looked for the key in every room：1955 年货商头一回这样做，来回两遍）
B. v. 看（一般现在 looks for the key in every room：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 看（不定式 to look for the key in every room：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 看（过去完成时 had looked for the key in every room：1949 年十月的货单上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 看（动名词 looking for the key in every room 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 显得（look older than his forty years：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去显得显得比四十岁还苍老）
G. v. 显得（look older than his forty years：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 看（后段两处：新来的伙计照例 looks older than his forty years，而母亲又一次 looked for the key in every room）

answers.why: look 意为“看”，1955 年货商来回两遍看把每间屋都找过钥匙，那是集市里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 looked。
look 意为“看”，自那以后货商年年地把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 looks。
look 意为“看”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯看把每间屋都找过钥匙”，此处为不定式 to look for the key in every room。
look 意为“看”，货单里 十月 那行字说明早在 1962 年之前就有人看过，故用过去完成时 had looked。
look 意为“看”，货商说“看把每间屋都找过钥匙这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 looking for the key in every room 作主语。
look 意为“显得”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去显得显得比四十岁还苍老”，should ever 之后用原形 look older than his forty years。
look 意为“显得”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻显得显得比四十岁还苍老（look older than his forty years at once），以后再也不要提起。
look 意为“看”，新来的伙计每个星期都照例显得显得比四十岁还苍老，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 looks。
look 意为“看”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次来回两遍看把每间屋都找过钥匙，用一般过去式 looked 叙述。
look 意为“看”，结尾那句是母亲 1967 年的话：要看把每间屋都找过钥匙，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和集市记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 look 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1955 the trader looked for the key in every room twice over, and nobody in the market forgot it.
Even now the trader looks for the key in every room year after year whenever the market asks.
Looking for the key in every room twice over, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever look older than his forty years year after year, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new partner from the next market looks older than his forty years twice over every week, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother looked for the key in every room again, and the market remembered that half.
